key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, and hand swelling
Ulcerated lichenoid papules on palmar IP creases
Oxford Scale muscle strength 5 of 5 throughout
Lymphocytopenia with CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL
Normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, and tissue thromboplastin
Chest CT showed hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities
Pulmonary function tests showed restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted)

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, and a 50-pound weight loss, combined with laboratory findings of elevated ferritin, depressed creatine kinase, lymphocytopenia, and positive anti-SSA (Ro) and anticardiolipin antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). The presence of hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities on Chest CT, as well as restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity on pulmonary function tests, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of mixed connective tissue disease, such as arthralgias and interstitial lung disease, the presence of positive anti-SSA (Ro) and anticardiolipin antibodies, as well as the pattern of organ involvement, are more consistent with SLE.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's normal muscle strength and lack of significant muscle enzyme elevation make dermatomyositis less likely, despite the presence of skin manifestations such as ulcerated lichenoid papules.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient has interstitial lung disease, the presence of systemic symptoms and autoantibodies suggests a more complex autoimmune disorder such as SLE, rather than a primary pulmonary disease.

rejected.label: Pulmonary Hypertension
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of pulmonary hypertension in the provided case facts, making this diagnosis less likely.
